PagerDuty Bot: :rotating_light: Incident PD-87623 created - multiple heartbeat alerts firing for embeddings-service (eu-west-1). Severity: P3. link=https://pd.example/company/incidents/PD-87623

Maya: saw this at 09:12 UTC. Lots of heartbeats flapping across the synthetic fleet: synth-heartbeat-eu-1/2/3 all triggered within a 2m window. No 5xx from production traces, just spikey RTT on the synth probes (p99 ~ 650ms).

Cheng: looking at the telemetry now. The probes hit a burst of elevated tail latency immediately after the 09:05 deploy of embeddings-v2.1.2. I can repro the spike in staging if I sweep requests at ~200qps.

Maya: can we confirm customer impact? I checked some product dashboards and there are small p95 bumps on embeddings calls but no errors. Likely noise from model warmup/kv cache churn.

Ravi: agreed — customers not reporting errors, most traffic fine. Recommend: 1) debounce the heartbeat rule to reduce false positives, 2) temporarily widen thresholds while we validate, 3) add a short suppression window to avoid repeated pages.

Maya: proposed quick mitigation: set alert to 'firing if p99 > 500ms for 3/5 windows' -> de-emphasize single-window flaps. Anyone object? :thinking_face:

Sam B: +1. Also suggest adding a secondary condition that checks error-rate < 0.1% so we don't suppress real failures.

Cheng: I'll open a PR for the Grafana alert rule. Draft rule change (pseudocode):

```
# grafana alert rule: embeddings_synth_heartbeat_latency
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="synth-heartbeat",region="eu-west-1"}[5m])) by (le))
for: 10m
annotations:
  description: "p99 heartbeat latency for embeddings synth probes"
conditions:
  - when: result > 500ms
  - and: increase(count_over_time(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="synth-heartbeat"}[5m]) > 5)
```

Cheng: basically require sustained tail latency plus a minimum number of high-bucket hits. That should cut single-sample noise.

Maya: what's the quickest way to suppress the current alert storms while we merge? Can we add a 30m muting rule for that alert group?

Ravi: yes - we can create a temporary mute in Alertmanager: `curl -XPOST $ALERTMGR/api/v2/silences -d '{"matchers": [{"name":"alertname","value":"embeddings_synth_heartbeat_latency"}], "startsAt":"2026-03-15T09:15:00Z", "endsAt":"2026-03-15T09:45:00Z", "comment":"temporary deglitch while we tune thresholds"}'`

Maya: doing it now. Silence created - ID S-8942. I'll document it in the incident timeline.

PagerDuty Bot: Incident PD-87623 acknowledged by Maya. On-call: Sam B (primary).

Sam B: taking on-call. Handoff: Maya — what else is outstanding?

Maya: outstanding: Cheng's PR to adjust rule (target + testing in staging), a dashboard we should pin for the post-incident review that shows: p99/p95, request rate, deploy events, and a 'probe-flap' counter we can compute as distinct synth endpoints firing in a 5m window. Also Marina asked for a short-term change to probe frequency to avoid synchronized bursts.

Marina (DSA): for the probe frequency change, suggestion: add jitter and increase interval from 30s -> 90s for eu probes for the next 2h. Example config snippet for the synth runner (YAML):

```
probes:
  - name: synth-heartbeat-eu-*
    interval: 90s
    jitter: 0.3   # 30% jitter
    timeout: 5s
    check: "/health/heartbeat"
```

Marina: jitter spreads the probe schedule so we avoid all probes hitting at the same time post-deploy.

Sam B: ok, make that change in the running runner (k8s config) as a hotfix and roll back after 2h. Who can apply?

Cheng: I can patch the k8s ConfigMap and trigger a rolling restart of the synth-runner in eu-west-1. Patch I plan to apply: `kubectl -n synth patch configmap probes --patch-file patch.yaml` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/synth-runner -n synth --selector=region=eu-west-1`

Maya: I'll handle external comms if needed. Note for customer impact: we'll keep product PGs informed if tail latency doesn't settle. So far, risk is low.

Ravi: to avoid repeated pages long-term, proposal for post-incident: 1) implement deglitch function in alerting (suppress single-window spikes), 2) add composite alert requiring both latency and error-rate or increased drop rate, 3) build a dashboard panel that highlights probe synchronization (heatmap of probe start times), 4) run a canary test with randomized probe jitter for a day.

Sam B: +1. Also add an automated playbook step: when we see X distinct synth endpoints alerting within 3m, escalate to SRE only if errors > 0.5% or request failures exist.

Maya: Cheng - assign the PR to me and Sam for quick review. Create a small runbook snippet in ops/heartbeat/README.md with the mitigation steps (silence, widen threshold, add jitter, revert).

Cheng: PR opened: https://git.example/repo/infra/graphs/pulls/1228 - includes Grafana rule, Alertmanager test, and runbook updates. Testing in staging now.

Sam B: after PR merges: please deploy rule and we should monitor for 30m. If stable, remove the silence and revert probe frequency back to normal over a 15m ramp.

Maya: we've applied the k8s patch, synth-runner pods restarted at 09:28 UTC. Observing metrics...

Grafana Bot: Alert rule embeddings_synth_heartbeat_latency -> resolved at 09:33 UTC (silenced).

Cheng: staging runs look clean with the new rule and jitter. Opening a follow-up ticket for 'heartbeat deglitch epic' to roll this across regions and add the dashboard: TRACK-5421.

Ravi: FYI I'll add a short-term dashboard panel to the incident board showing: number of distinct synth endpoints firing in last 5m, p99 latency, deployments in last hour. That will help PMs and oncall triage next time.

Maya: handoff complete to Sam B. I'll remain reachable if anything flares.

Sam B: thanks — I'll keep watch for 60m and then sign off if stable. Action items summary: [Cheng] finish PR & merge, [Maya] document silence + external note, [Marina] coordinate probe config change and rollback plan, [Ravi] create dashboard panel, [Sam B] monitor 60m then close incident.

Sam B: closing PD incident on my side after 60m of stable metrics unless someone objects. :thumbsup:

Maya: no objections. Good catch. We'll follow up with a brief post-incident writeup focusing on alert rule deglitch patterns and probe scheduling.

PagerDuty Bot: PD-87623: Incident resolved by Sam B at 10:20 UTC.
